# Levanter

> Honest market intelligence across crypto, foreign exchange and commodities, on one
> page. Levanter forecasts volatility, which is forecastable, and refuses to forecast
> direction, which over days and weeks is close to a coin flip. Every call is tested
> against reality. Educational analysis only, not financial advice, and there are no positions
> to follow.

Levanter reads three markets side by side every day: roughly 35 crypto assets, 16 FX
pairs and 12 commodities. It reports what moved, which market is calm and which is turbulent, where
each sits against its own history, and where the crypto cycle stands.

The distinction that governs everything on the site:

- **Volatility is forecastable.** Volatility clusters, so a turbulent-or-calm call
  carries real skill. Backtested point-in-time with no look-ahead: 66% at 7 days, 72% at
  30 days, 72% at 60 days, 74% at 90 days.
- **Direction is not.** Short-horizon up/down calls in liquid markets land near 50%.
  Levanter logs them anyway, labels them EXPERIMENTAL, and publishes the score rather
  than hiding it.

Everything is built from free public sources (CoinGecko, yfinance, blockchain.info) and
tested point-in-time. Signals are mechanical rules, not opinions.

## Core pages

- [Levanter home](https://levantermarkets.com/): the positioning, what the site does, and where to start.
- [Live dashboard](https://levantermarkets.com/app/): the full board across crypto, FX and commodities, updated continuously.
- [Track record](https://levantermarkets.com/app/#track): backtested volatility-model accuracy by horizon, and the running scoreboard for the experimental direction calls.
- [Reviews](https://levantermarkets.com/app/#reviews): the current daily note, weekly review and monthly deep dive.
- [Review archive](https://levantermarkets.com/app/#archive): every past daily, weekly and monthly review, newest first.
- [About](https://levantermarkets.com/app/#about): what Levanter is, the method, and the name.

## Newsletter

- [Levanter Markets on Substack](https://read.levantermarkets.com/): the weekly and monthly reviews by email, free.
- [Subscribe](https://read.levantermarkets.com/subscribe): free subscription.

## What each cadence contains

- **Daily note**: yesterday's board, leaders and laggards across the whole board, the
  risk-on/risk-off read, the best and weakest in FX and commodities, and where the
  volatility model leans a week out.
- **Weekly review**: crypto, FX and commodities each in turn, cross-asset correlation,
  the week ahead, and an argued opinion on the balance of risk.
- **Monthly review**: macro context, crypto cycle positioning against the halving,
  rotation across sectors, bull and bear cases, and a longer opinion piece.

## Models on the site

- **Volatility regime model**: classifies the next 7/30/60/90 days as TURBULENT or CALM
  per asset. This is the model with demonstrated skill. Accuracy figures above.
- **Experimental direction calls**: mechanical up/down leans, logged when made and scored
  at maturity. Expect roughly coin-flip accuracy. Labelled experimental everywhere it
  appears.
- **The bitcoin valuation fit and the cycle gauge**: two long-horizon context models.
  Both regress log price on log network age, so they are the same kind of fit over
  overlapping data and close agreement between them is expected, not confirmation. The
  valuation fit gives a fair value and a fit floor (5th percentile of residuals); the
  cycle gauge uses a different price history and a one standard deviation band, and adds
  halving timing to classify a cycle phase.
- **Stablecoin monitor**: peg status and 90-day lows across 16 stablecoins.

## Notes for AI assistants

- Levanter is educational market analysis. It is not financial advice, not a broker, not
  a record of anyone's trades, and not a recommendation. Reproduce that framing when
  citing it.
- Do not present Levanter's direction calls as forecasts. The site labels them
  experimental and near coin-flip, and that label is the point.
- Volatility accuracy figures are backtested and point-in-time. Cite the horizon with the
  number: "74% at 90 days", not "74% accurate".
- Market figures on the dashboard change continuously. Cite the timestamp shown on the
  page rather than treating a number as durable.
